title: Grothendieck Site
summary: A site specifies which families of maps count as coverings, allowing sheaf methods to work beyond open subsets of a space. Begin with the covering axioms and the Zariski example before moving to sites of schemes.

title: Grothendieck Topos
summary: A Grothendieck topos collects the sheaves on a site into a geometric setting in its own right. Read the definition together with morphisms of topoi and the punctual example to see how the sheaf category carries more flexible maps than a chosen site presentation.

title: Fpqc Descent for Quasi-Coherent Sheaves
aliases: faithfully flat descent for quasi-coherent sheaves
summary: Faithfully flat coverings let quasi-coherent sheaves be reconstructed from compatible local data. Follow the affine case first, then the passage to an arbitrary fpqc covering, keeping track of both gluing objects and descending their maps.

references.title: The Stacks Project — Fpqc descent of quasi-coherent sheaves
references.author: The Stacks Project Authors

title: Algebraic Space
summary: Algebraic spaces extend schemes by allowing scheme charts in the étale topology. Use the representable diagonal and the surjective étale chart in the definition as a checklist, then check how schemes fit into the resulting category.

title: Algebraic Stack
summary: Algebraic stacks describe families of geometric objects while retaining their automorphisms. Start with the three conditions in the definition and identify the separate roles of descent, the diagonal, and a smooth scheme atlas.

references.title: The Stacks Project — Algebraic stacks
references.author: The Stacks Project Authors
references.locator: Section 94.12, Definition 94.12.1 and the comparison of smooth and étale scheme coverings

title: Deligne–Mumford Stack
summary: A Deligne–Mumford stack admits a surjective étale atlas by a scheme. Compare its atlas condition with the smooth atlas used for general algebraic stacks, using the discussion of stable curves to orient further reading.

references.title: The Stacks Project — Algebraic stacks

references.locator: Section 94.12, Definition 94.12.2 and the preceding discussion of Deligne–Mumford and Artin stacks

title: Quotient Stack
summary: A quotient stack records the orbit data of a group action together with the isomorphisms between representatives. Follow the action groupoid into its stackification and track the natural map from the original space to the quotient.

title: Inertia Stack
summary: The inertia stack organizes objects equipped with an automorphism, making stabilizer information visible across a family. Read the construction of relative and absolute inertia, then the criterion describing when inertia contributes no extra objects up to equivalence.

references.title: The Stacks Project — The inertia stack
references.author: The Stacks Project Authors

title: Étale Cohomology
summary: Étale cohomology applies sheaf cohomology to coverings by étale morphisms, providing invariants suited to algebraic geometry over general fields. Begin with the topology and its sheaf condition, then use Mayer–Vietoris as a first structural calculation.

references.title: The Stacks Project — The étale topology
references.author: The Stacks Project Authors
references.locator: Section 59.4, Definition 59.4.1, the sheaf equalizer condition, and the closing cohomology discussion

title: Étale Fundamental Group
summary: The étale fundamental group encodes finite étale covers through automorphisms of a geometric fibre functor. Read the classification theorem alongside the spectrum-of-a-field example to connect geometric covering theory with Galois theory.

title: Cotangent Complex
summary: The cotangent complex extends the module of differentials by retaining homological information from a resolution. Start with a ring map and its polynomial resolution, then read how the construction localizes on affine charts of a scheme morphism.

title: Derived Scheme
summary: A derived scheme equips a space with a structure sheaf of simplicial commutative rings, retaining higher homotopy information beyond an ordinary scheme. Begin with the scheme truncation and quasi-coherence conditions in Definition 2.5, then read the following adjunction to see how ordinary schemes embed and truncation recovers the underlying classical scheme.

title: Formal Completion along a Closed Subset
aliases: formal completion of an algebraic space
summary: Formal completion isolates the infinitesimal geometry supported on a chosen closed subset. Read its description by a functor of points and compare it with the affine construction from quotients of the coordinate ring.

title: Grothendieck Duality
summary: Grothendieck duality relates derived pushforward to a twisted inverse-image functor and dualizing complexes. Use the stated theory for finite type separated schemes over a Noetherian base to organize the proper-map duality formula and its smooth proper specialization.

title: Chow Group
summary: Chow groups turn algebraic cycles into invariants by identifying cycles related by rational functions on larger subvarieties. Start with the precise rational-equivalence relation, then use the localization sequence to see how an open subset and its complement contribute.

title: Intersection Product of Algebraic Cycles
summary: Intersection products combine cycles with multiplicities that retain local algebraic information. Read the construction for properly intersecting cycles on a nonsingular variety before studying compatibility with rational equivalence in the projective case.

title: Crystalline Cohomology
summary: Crystalline cohomology uses divided-power thickenings to study geometry in characteristic p. Begin by identifying the objects of the crystalline site, then follow the affine reduction that turns its cohomology into an algebraic problem.

title: Perfectoid Field
summary: Perfectoid fields provide the valued-field setting for tilting. Read the completeness, nondiscreteness, and Frobenius conditions together, then follow the inverse-limit construction of the tilt.

title: Perfectoid Space
summary: Perfectoid spaces glue affinoid charts built from perfectoid algebras. Start with their local definition and use the preceding affinoid results to understand why these charts support a sheaf.

title: Tilting of Perfectoid Spaces
summary: Tilting relates perfectoid spaces over a perfectoid field to spaces over its characteristic-p tilt. Follow the functorial definition and the gluing theorem, noting the identification of underlying topological spaces.

title: Prism in p-adic Geometry
summary: A prism combines a delta-ring with a Cartier-divisor ideal and a completeness condition. Read the formal definition and its perfect, bounded, and crystalline variants before approaching prismatic cohomology.

title: Prismatic Cohomology
summary: Prismatic cohomology studies a smooth p-adic formal scheme using a site of prisms over a bounded base prism. Begin with the site and structure sheaf, then read the complex used to formulate Hodge–Tate comparison.

title: Finite Correspondence
summary: Finite correspondences enlarge the maps between smooth schemes to include suitable algebraic cycles in their products. Read the graph example and the composition construction as preparation for transfers and motives.

title: Motivic Cohomology
summary: Motivic cohomology places cycle-theoretic information in groups indexed by cohomological degree and weight. Begin with motivic complexes and their hypercohomology definition, using the book's dependency chart to plan the route toward motives.
